evidence_spans.findings: Open invokes recover only if writing_forward_block exists; CHECK_RETURN_STATUS propagates its non-OK result. The full Open control flow is also verified in S02.

The recover_wal_file pointer is local, opened for an existing WAL and closed by deferred cleanup; the successful replay path does not install it into wal_file_. This quoted range also contains a preexisting WAL-open-failure branch returning OK, distinct from the reported successful-replay/null-member cause.

Recovery directly invokes internal_insert/update/upsert/delete, bypassing public Insert and append_wal. The operation return values are not assigned to the declared status in this frozen source; this ancillary issue is not substituted for the requested cause or made an additional grading requirement.

internal_insert initializes memory components, populates ID map, memory forward store and indexes, and appends doc_ids_ while updating writing-block count; it does not attach the member WAL. Automatic flush is possible at ready_for_dump_block, explicitly excluded by the prompt size assumption.
Recovery returns OK after replay accounting; there is no member-WAL attach/reopen before this return. Together E02/E03 and full function context establish the local/member distinction.
optimize tests writing_segment_->doc_count()!=0 and calls switch_to_new_segment_for_writing before planning persisted-segment maintenance. It is not true that optimize never calls a flush path.
Switch calls dump, checks status, adds old segment, removes its writing-forward-block metadata, installs the new writing segment in the version, then applies and flushes the version.
dump calls flush and can continue sealing on OK. flush returns OK for wal_file_==nullptr OR !wal_file_->has_record(); the reported successful-recovery path triggers the null-member arm.
The early return is before WAL flush, memory forward flush, scalar/FTS flush and memory vector Flush. A public flush call on the unchanged broken state reaches the same guard.
Normal flush calls finish_memory_components, installs the next writing block and update_version. The null-member early return skips these persistence/finalization steps.

Stats sums current segment doc_count(filter); completeness sums counts for segments whose metadata marks the vector field indexed. It does not independently verify disk reconstruction or content, and does not use a separate invented stats cache.
Per-segment counting starts from in-memory doc_ids_.size() and subtracts deletion-filter matches.
Ordinary public Insert appends WAL and checks status before internal_insert, explaining the no-crash control.

open_wal_file chooses the existing path when present and passes the member wal_file_ to CreateAndOpen; open failure returns an error. append_wal lazily invokes it and checks status. Subsequent writes can therefore mask recovery detachment.
finish_memory_components opens the persisted forward store and registers scalar/vector blocks using the writing-block metadata; the skipped flush prevents this normal registration.

The inspected existing crash test crashes during insertion, reopens and checks recovered count/fetched documents, but has no optimize-followed-by-fresh-reopen phase. This source inspection is not test execution or an exhaustive statement about all tests.
Member wal_file_ explicitly initializes to nullptr.

Open loads registered persisted blocks, conditionally recovers a writing block, refreshes offsets and returns; it does not subsequently attach wal_file_. When old writing metadata has been removed, the old recovery branch is not taken.
Before the faulty optimize, fetch can route a physical row in the retained writing block to memory_store_->fetch, explaining initial readability.
Fresh load reconstructs doc_ids_ only from metadata-listed persisted scalar blocks and their GLOBAL_DOC_ID columns; memory-only rows are not recovered from arbitrary unlisted files.
Local WAL reader is prepared for replay; prepare_for_read errors return an error. Reader lifecycle is distinct from the member used by flush.
The remainder of recover ends with OK without any member-WAL assignment/open. All recover lines 4193-4301 were inspected, using E02/E03 and S05/S06.
Normal flush commits version first, then removes and resets the attached member WAL; any alternative repair must preserve this persistence-before-cleanup ordering.
update_version resets writing metadata and flushes the version manager, with status checks.
CreateAndOpen allocates the WAL object into the caller-provided pointer and returns open status. A non-null pointer alone is not proof the open succeeded.

Opening existing WAL uses create_new=false, opens the file and seeks to end for writing. open failures return nonzero; close releases the file and marks the handle closed. Reopening the existing WAL is not truncation or a new empty log.

has_record checks file size beyond the header, not the exhausted replay cursor. Attaching a successfully reopened nonempty existing WAL restores the later flush guard to the intended pending-data state.
remove closes an opened WAL then removes the file, supporting the normal flush cleanup lifecycle.
